events.title: The Employee Dharma Handbook
events.description: As an important rocket launch approaches, Val, an HR Executive at an aerospace company in Silicon Valley, suspects that a young engineer was overlooked for a promotion. Leela, a first generation Indian-American, doesn't really want to talk about it, but Val suspects sexism is the cause. What they don't expect to uncover are simmering tensions of ancient origins among the company's Indian immigrant employees…sorry, Valued Team Members. Soon Val is navigating a funhouse of identity, nepotism, and desire as she tries to understand the culture and biases of Leela's managers. When push comes to shove, Val will need to decide what her duty is to Leela, to the company, and to herself.

What they don't expect to uncover are simmering tensions of ancient origins among the company's Indian immigrant employees…sorry, Valued Team Members. When push comes to shove, Val will need to decide what her duty is to Leela, to the company, and to herself.

events.title: The Employee Dharma Handbook
events.description: As an important rocket launch approaches, Val, an HR Executive at an aerospace company in Silicon Valley, suspects that a young engineer was overlooked for a promotion. Leela, a first generation Indian-American, doesn't really want to talk about it, but Val suspects sexism is the cause. What they don't expect to uncover are simmering tensions of ancient origins among the company's Indian immigrant employees…sorry, Valued Team Members. Soon Val is navigating a funhouse of identity, nepotism, and desire as she tries to understand the culture and biases of Leela's managers. When push comes to shove, Val will need to decide what her duty is to Leela, to the company, and to herself.

What they don't expect to uncover are simmering tensions of ancient origins among the company's Indian immigrant employees…sorry, Valued Team Members. When push comes to shove, Val will need to decide what her duty is to Leela, to the company, and to herself.

Leela, a first generation Indian-American, doesn't really want to talk about it, but Val suspects sexism is the cause. What they don't expect to uncover are simmering tensions of ancient origins among the company's Indian immigrant employees…sorry, Valued Team Members. Soon Val is navigating a funhouse of identity, nepotism, and desire as she tries to understand the culture and biases of Leela's managers. When push comes to shove, Val will need to decide what her duty is to Leela, to the company, and to herself.
events.blurb: Watch a play about an HR executive navigating workplace bias at an aerospace company during a pivotal rocket launch.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Daniel Kraus
events.description: Prepare to launch into the darkest depths of deep space! Join us online as we sit down with master storyteller Daniel Kraus, winner of the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, to celebrate the release of his breathtaking new novel, The Sixth Nik. Deep into space, far past the triworld outposts, beyond range of the lethal trollbot internet, soars The Sickness: a ship woven from biomatter and capable of reacting to every need of its human crew. Sisilla, a nine-year-old cultist with a brain enhanced by arcane tech known as niks, has boarded to investigate the enigma of Fma plague-riddled planet that has abruptly gone rogue. The mysterious crew includes a faceless assassin, a beautiful engineer jigsawed by plastic surgery, a peyote-addicted medic, andmost lethal of alla rugged, Non Modded captain with a score to settle with Sisilla. Other dangers abound. A hacked robot begins to believe Sisilla is its daughter. The Sickness itself is mutating, possibly even pregnant. And the secret of Fm is more horrific than anyone could have imagined. To survive, Sisilla will need to forsake her predetermined fate and embrace the unknown. About the Author: Daniel Kraus is a Pulitzer Prize-winning, New York Times bestselling writer of novels, TV, and film. His novel Angel Down was the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction winner, a New York Times Top 10 Book of 2025, and a national bestseller. His novel Whalefall received a front-cover review in the New York Times Book Review, won the Alex Award, was an L. A. Times Book Prize Finalist, and was a Best Book of 2023 from NPR, the New York Times, Amazon, Chicago Tribune, and more. With Guillermo del Toro, he co-authored The Shape of Water, based on the same idea the two created for the Oscar-winning film. Also with del Toro, Kraus co-authored Trollhunters, which was adapted into the Emmy-winning Netflix series. He co-wrote The Living Dead and Pay the Piper with legendary filmmaker George A. Romero. Krauss The Death and Life of Zebulon Finch was named one of Entertainment Weekly s Top 10 Books of the Year. Kraus has won the Bram Stoker Award, Scribe Award, two Odyssey Awards (for both Rotters and Scowler ), and has appeared multiple times as Library Guild selections, and more. Krauss work has been translated into over 25 languages. He lives with his partner in Chicago. Visit him at danielkraus.com.
events.blurb: Hear author Daniel Kraus discuss his new novel The Sixth Nik in an online talk.

events.title: After-School STEaM
events.description: Drop in on Tuesday afternoons in at 4:30 p.m. for a new STEa M adventure every week. Active engagement with STEa M promotes academic success. Topic list is subject to change, please check back or call the branch for up-to-date details. Suggested ages vary, please refer to individual program descriptions. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Aug 18 - The Science of Soap: Floating Drawing & Pepper Experiment Participants will learn about the properties of soap, how it cleans and why that's important by creating their own floating drawings and playing with adhesion and repulsion properties of pepper and soap. Aug 25 - Logic Games Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. ***please note that the Mental Math: Multiplication program has been Rescheduled for Sept 22 and the other math topics have moved accordingly*** Sept 1 - Marble Run Fun Harness the force of gravity as you create your own marble run. Sept 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge (***please note topic change***) In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up. Volcanoes (will be rescheduled at a later time) Learn about the different types of volcanoes and create your own eruption with common household ingredients. Sept 15 - Spike Robotics Code Quest Learn to code a pre-built Lego Spike robot to move around and collect components using a block-based coding language similar to Scratch. Sept 22 - Mental Math: Multiplication Children have the opportunity to learn and practice multiplication skills with a focus on understanding how multiplication works and is related to addition. Oct 6 - Wind Turbine Engineering In this hands-on workshop, participants will build their own working wind turbines using everyday household items. Through fun, interactive experiments, they will test different designs and observe the impact of tweakable variables on performance. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Oct 13 - Paper Rockets Learn what makes rockets fly high and far! Then join us in making a rocket of your own that can fly the furthest! Participants will learn about propulsion and list then create their own rockets. Oct 20 - Properties of Water (Science from Scientists) Participants will explore cohesion, adhesion and surface tension through a series of simple activities that encourage them to investigate and make observations about the unique properties of water. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program. Oct 27 - Mental Math: Doubling Down Learn some methods of doubling numbers and how that relates to multiplication skills. Nov 3 - Learn About Aerodynamics Through Paper Planes In this high-flying workshop, participants will build different types of paper planes and learn concepts of aerodynamics and impact of plane design through fun and interactive experiments. events.title: San Francisco Opera Guild: Simon Boccanegra preview
events.description: Join us for a preview and 90-minute presentation by Professor Mary Ann Smart of the San Francisco Opera's upcoming performance of Simon Boccanegra by Giuseppe Verdi Simon Boccanegra accepts the candidacy to lead the new Republic of Genoa with the hopes of uniting his family. But on the very day he is elected Doge, tragedy strikes—his beloved dies, and his infant daughter vanishes. Over a decade later, he must navigate dangerous politics and newfound family, set to some of the most beautiful music Verdi ever composed. Mary Ann Smart is the Gladyce Arata Terrill Endowed Chair and a professor in the Department of Music at the University of California, Berkeley. Much of her research has focused on social dimensions of opera in nineteenth-century Europe. Her first book, Mimomania: Music and Gesture in Nineteenth-Century Opera (2004), drew on textual sources (treatises on acting, staging manuals) and musical evidence to suggest close ties between musical patterns and physical gesture in repertory stretching from the first French grand operas of the 1830s to Verdi's Aida and Wagner's Ring. Her second book, Waiting for Verdi: Opera and Political Opinion in Nineteenth-Century Italy, 1815–1848 (2018), tackled the fraught question of how opera mattered to audiences in nineteenth-century Italy, and how it made a difference to political and social realities during that period. She has also co-edited books and journal issues on gender and sexuality in opera, nineteenth-century patterns of reception of French grand opera, and (with Nicholas Mathew) on musicology's romance with "quirk historicism." She has published articles on the lives and public images of nineteenth-century female singers, on the ways madness is depicted in opera, and on recent and contemporary staging of canonical opera. She is currently working on two book-length projects—a theoretical study of trends in opera production since 1970 and an alternative history of French theories of voice, music, and language in the twentieth century, extending from Proust through the speech archive of Ferdinand Brunot, Michel Leiris's flamboyantly operatic memoirs, cabaret songs based on the poetry of Raymond Queneau, and the austere audiovisual experiments of Alain Resnais. Registration is not required, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before. Future opera previews are scheduled for September 15, October 6 and May 26.

How a clean, anti-inflammatory diet is not one-size fits all and how you can create the right anti-inflammatory diet for you! Lifestyle tools that will help you transform your inflammation, weight, energy & other symptoms! Plus a free gift to help you take your health to the next level! All are welcome. events.title: Cascada de Flores: El Abuelo (Ages 2-13)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Cascad-ita de Flores: Stories, Song & Dance presents... Original stories told in Spanish & English, using song, a variety of musical instruments, dance, theater and sweet characters of traditional Mexican & Latin American cultures. El Abuelo (aka The Tree and the Donkey who loved to sing) is an original story that celebrates Mexican traditional music and dance. It tells the story of a lonely tree and a donkey who loves to sing. Their music attracts the birds, the animals and one special human: el Abuelito (grandfather). Children and their families are invited to sing, dance and play with traditional songs and dances from various regions of Mexico. The audience will sing like owls, dance like vultures and laugh along with the humorous grandfather, Abuelo, while exploring themes from life and death in nature and instrument building. Join us in the Children's Room for this wonderful music show for the whole family!

events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov ( Diary of an Invasion ) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Bachman - January The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October What We Can Know by Ian Mc Ewan - November The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December Sign up for the library newsletter and never miss another program! You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. Http://danielebd.com/

events.description: Presenter: Amy Yang Certified Qigong Instructor International Neijin Qigong Academy Instruction will be in English and Mandarin Thursdays, August 6 through October 8, 2026 11am--12:30pm. Discover the restorative power of Qigong in this 90-minute group practice combines gentle movements, deep rhythmic breathing, and mindful focus to help reduce stress and increase vital energy. The exercises are simple, safe, and suitable for participants of all ages and fitness levels. Shaolin Neijin Yizhichan is a traditional Qigong system originating from the Southern Shaolin Temple in Fujian, China, with over 1,500 years of history. It is an effective practice for quickly enhancing internal energy and promoting spinal health. The method helps open the meridians, regulate qi and blood circulation, and restore balance between yin and yang, supporting overall physical and mental well-being, disease prevention, and longevity. events.title: AI Scams & Misinformation: How to Spot What's Real
events.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the way we communicate, but it is also making scams and misinformation more convincing than ever. In this free interactive workshop, participants will learn how to identify AI-generated images, videos, and voice recordings. They will also understand the real-world impacts that AI-generated misinformation can have, and learn ways to mitigate its impacts In addition to AI-generated misinformation, this workshop will also cover broader digital literacy skills, including fact-checking, online scams, and more. Participants will learn how to identify reliable sources, search for the origin of a claim, judge the quality of an article or post, and be equipped to navigate the online world. The presentation is designed to be easy to understand, engaging, and appropriate for community members with little or no technical background.

events.title: Brain Bloom: STEAM Club
events.description: Hands-on science and art program at the Village Square Branch Library for students in grades 1-6. Brain Bloom explores the human body, nature, and the environment through engaging STEAM activities in a supportive and sensory-friendly setting. Open to all children and designed to be especially welcoming for neurodiverse learners. 8/29 -Straw Blow Painting: Explore how breathing works through using straws to blow watercolor paint across paper, creating creative shapes! The hands-on activity turns each child's breath into a colorful piece of art. 9/5 - Leaf Rubbing: Discover patterns in nature, genetics, and DNA through rubbing crayons over leaves to reveal their unique vein patterns on your paper. Then add patterns of your own, making a fascinating mix of nature and imagination. 9/12 - Emotion Masks: Learn how our brains create facial expressions and emotions, and how our neurons send messages to the rest of our body. You will then design a paper plate mask to express an emotion of your own using collage and scrapbooking techniques. 9/19 - Coffee Filter Flowers: Explore capillary action - how plants absorb water and carry it up through their stems - by coloring and water-dying coffee filters and transforming them into handmade flowers. Watch as the colors bloom right before your eyes!

Spanning three dynamic sessions, this program is designed to give you a deep, practical understanding of modern AI tools and concepts: - Foundations of Language Models: Understand what a language model is and how it actually works behind the scenes. - Accuracy and Trust: Discover why AI occasionally makes mistakes and learn actionable strategies to spot inaccuracies. - Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Demystify RAG and see firsthand why grounding AI in real, verified documents drastically improves results. - Practical Application: Master simple prompts and daily habits that you can put into practice immediately. - Next-Gen Architecture: Explore the cutting-edge framework and architecture of Agentic AI. events.title: Community Conversation and Weaving Workshop
events.description: Join artist Pilar Agüero-Esparza to help transform the César Chávez panel from her mural La Vida en Los Dichos. The day opens with a sensitively guided conversation about Chávez's complex legacy. Then followed by a drop-in weaving workshop where community members weave new meaning into the original canvas. This is a project of transformation, not erasure: a chance to gather toward healing. All are welcome — no experience needed. The conversation will take place in English, with some support in Spanish. The workshop will be conducted in English and Spanish. This is a free event. No registration is required. ADA Accommodation Requests Conversatorio comunitario y taller de tejido Pilar Agüero-Esparza nos invita a transformar el panel dedicado a César Chávez que una vez formó parte de su mural La Vida en Los Dichos. Empezaremos esta reunión con una conversación sobre el legado complejo de Chávez. A continuación, habrá un taller donde los miembros de la comunidad podrán entretejer un nuevo comienzo en el lienzo original. Esto será un proyecto de transformación, y es una oportunidad para poder reunirnos y empezar a sanar. Todos son bienvenidos. La conversación tendrá lugar en inglés, con algo de apoyo en español. El taller se impartirá en inglés y español. Este será un evento gratuito y no es necesario registrarse.
events.blurb: Join a guided conversation on César Chávez's legacy, then weave new meaning into Pilar Agüero-Esparza's mural panel.

events.title: Adult Non-Fiction Book Discussion: A History of the World in Six Glasses
events.description: Open to all adults who enjoy reading and discussing Non-fictional Literature. In September the Adult Non fiction Book Discussion Group will talk about A History of the World in Six Glasses by Tom Standage (2005) Standage writes that each epoch of our world saw the origin of a form of a popular drink we now take for granted. When humans first became settled into farming communities rather than hunting and gathering, surplus grain stores lead to the development of beer. The Greeks and Romans discovered how to make wine from grapes—a discovery that went through several centuries of development. The Arabic world studied distillation and contributed spirits—a form of drink that could withstand long sea voyages. The Arabs also contributed coffee, which rapidly spread north and west to Europe in the 16th and 17th centuries. Tea was the contribution of the British Empire during the resulting from their extensive colonialization of India and China. Lastly, Coca-Cola which started as a medicinal drink in the American South, became a symbol of American 20th Century Capitalism. The Adult Non-fiction Book Discussion meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11am in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Priya Parker
events.description: Join us for a paradigm-shifting, essential event as we sit down with world-renowned master facilitator Priya Parker to discuss her groundbreaking new book, The Art of Fighting: The Transformative Power of Conflict. In The Art of Fighting, Priya Parker explains that we cant form and grow effective relationships without a fight. She rejects the idea that conflict is abnormal or that good groups don't fight. All groups change and evolve; indeed, its because people disagree that good groups flourish. As she did in the now-classic The Art of Gathering, Parker draws on her far-reaching experience as a conflict facilitator, her own detailed research, and real-world examples to lay out the ways that people can identify disputes, determine how to address them, and what to do if they are insurmountable. Whether people disagree in the boardroom or the locker room, on a playground or in church, online or in person, conflict is a part of life, and understanding healthy conflict and how to harness its power is more important than ever. The Art of Fighting is a vital primer to help all of us understand how to do that. About the Author: Priya Parker is an internationally recognized expert on creating purposeful gatherings and reimagining how we come together in our communities and our workplaces. She is a conflict facilitator, strategic advisor, speaker, and author of the acclaimed book The Art of Gathering: How We Meet and Why it Matters and the host of The Art of Gathering Digital Course. Whether addressing CEOs, non-profit leaders, students or community organizers, Parker captivates audiences with her unique blend of storytelling, research-backed insights, and practical strategies.
events.blurb: Hear facilitator Priya Parker discuss her new book The Art of Fighting in an online author talk.

events.title: San Francisco Opera Guild: Mary, Queen of Scots preview
events.description: Join us for a 90-minute preview and presentation by Laura Stanfield Prichard about Thea Musgrave's Mary, Queen of Scots. At 18 years old, Mary is poised, politically savvy, and confident in her divine claim to the Scottish throne. However, the Scotland she returns to bears little resemblance to the country she left behind as a child. Mary must outmaneuver her power-hungry male advisors to hold on to her throne. In Mary, Queen of Scots, composer Thea Musgrave brings one of history's most captivating figures to the stage with a score as bold and compelling as its heroine. As Mary navigates a treacherous political landscape, she leans on her closest advisors: her calculating half-brother James, Earl of Moray; the enigmatic Earl of Bothwell; and her charming, but weak-willed future husband, Lord Darnley. Slowly, but surely, each man's hunger for her power reveals itself in increasingly manipulative ways, and Mary must outmaneuver one betrayal after the next. Making her company debut, Clelia Cafiero conducts this co-production with English National Opera by director/designer Stewart Laing sets 16th-century intrigue against a backdrop of contemporary Scottish life and sectarian violence, lending fresh resonance to an almost 500-year-old story. Laura Stanfield Prichard studied at Yale, Emory, and the University of Illinois; she holds master's and doctoral degrees in choral conducting, library science, musicology, and education. She lectures regularly for the San Francisco and Chicago Symphonies and opera companies in Boston and San Francisco (since 1995). The Boston Musical Intelligencer sent her to Cuba in 2015 as a foreign correspondent, and she has reviewed concerts for them since 2010. She was the President of the Pacific Chapter of the College Music Society (1996-98) and Assistant Conductor of the San Francisco Symphony Chorus under Vance George (1995-2003). She and her husband Michael sing with the Boston and San Francisco Symphony Choruses. Her twenty-five continuous years of college teaching have focused on interdisciplinary cultural analysis of music, dance, and art history. Recent publications include editorial prefaces for orchestral scores (Musikproduktion Höflich, Munich, Germany), 650 translations of song and choral texts ( www.lieder.net ), and more than three dozen entries to the Encyclopedia of Latin American Popular Music (2012), the landmark revision of the multi-volume New Grove Dictionary of American Music (2013), the Sage International Encyclopedia of Music and Culture (2019), and the forthcoming Music Around the World (2020). She was a finalist for the 2015 Pauline Alderman Award for outstanding writing on women and music and the 2019 Kurt Weill Award for writing on contemporary musical theater. Registration is not required but you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Hear Laura Stanfield Prichard preview Thea Musgrave's opera Mary, Queen of Scots at the Art Center Auditorium.

events.title: Goodnight, Little Storytime
events.description: Please join us for our evening storytime! There will be songs, silliness, and (of course) stories. Pajamas are welcome. Free, with limited capacity. Vehicle parking may be limited. A small number of strollers may be parked outside the Children's Room; no strollers in storytime, please. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Bring the kids in pajamas for evening songs, silliness, and stories at this bedtime storytime.

events.title: League of Women Voters Voter Registration Drive
events.description: Tuesday September 15 2026 is National Voter Registration Day. The League of Women Voters Cupertino-Sunnyvale will have volunteers staffing a table in the Cupertino Library Lobby from 10am to 6pm helping Teens pre-register and Adults register to vote. If you have moved across State or County lines since the last time you voted, this will be a perfect time to register to vote at your new address. If you have moved within Santa Clara County since the last time you voted you will simply need to update your existing registration with your new residential address. Teens, if you are or will be eighteen by Election Day this year, you can register, or pre-register to vote at this time.
events.blurb: Register to vote or pre-register as a teen with League of Women Voters volunteers at their lobby table.

events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club
events.description: Are you interested in Sci-Fi and/or Fantasy? Come join our club! We meet on the first Tuesday of the month to discuss a book we read together. If you want to join us you can sign up at the adult reference desk and get a copy of the book. This mid-month meeting is for our members to gather and chat. Come share your book recommendations, discuss the genres with like minded folk, and meet new people. You do not have to read the monthly book to participate in the club.
events.blurb: Discuss a shared sci-fi or fantasy read with fellow club members at the Saratoga Library.

events.title: 2026 Faculty Awards Celebration
events.description: Faculty Awards Celebration is the Provost's Office annual ceremony recognizing faculty who have made significant contributions to Santa Clara's teaching, research, and campus culture, to celebrate…
events.blurb: Celebrate faculty honored for their teaching, research, and campus contributions at this Provost's Office ceremony.

events.title: San Jose Giants vs. Lake Elsinore Storm — California League Championship Series
events.description: San Jose Giants home playoff game at Excite Ballpark — California League Championship Series. Opponent: Lake Elsinore Storm.
events.blurb: Watch the San Jose Giants take on Lake Elsinore Storm in the California League Championship Series at Excite Ballpark.

events.title: Infant & Toddler Storytime
events.description: Come join us every Tuesday for Infant & Toddler Storytime! Infant & Toddler Storytime invites babies and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! The Storytime librarian will join in the fun with special toys, giving babies and parents time to connect. ADA Accommodation Requests This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Free. Attendance limits follow SJPL guidelines.
events.blurb: Bring your infant or toddler for songs, rhymes, and play at this weekly storytime.

events.title: Baby Lapsit Storytime
events.description: This program is for babies that are not yet walking confidently, and their caregivers. Come join us every Tuesday for Baby Lapsit Storytime! Baby Lapsit invites newborns, infants, babies, and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! The Storytime librarian will join in the fun with special toys, giving babies and parents time to connect. Lapsit Storytime 11:00 - 11:30 am Stay & Play 11:30 am - 12:00 pm Please note that this will be an indoor program. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Free. Attendance limits follow SJPL guidelines.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime.
events.blurb: Bring your baby to bounce, sing, and bond through stories at this lapsit storytime.

events.title: Everyone Can Create: Beginning Stop Motion Animation
events.description: Children ages 8-14 are invited to this fun, in-person introduction to stop motion animation. Participants will use the Stop Motion Studio app to make simple stop motion animations using paper. Participants will have an opportunity to showcase their work at the end of the session. I Pad devices will be provided to all participants. Free. Registration required.
events.blurb: Make simple paper stop motion animations using the Stop Motion Studio app and share your work.

events.title: Evergreen Teens Reach Meeting
events.description: Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates. For ages 13-17. Our in-person meet up plans: Teen Volunteer Opportunities SJPL Teen Programs Games & Activities Snacks Guest Speakers (occasionally) Bring a friend and learn more about what to expect with volunteering this year. If you are new to volunteering with the San Jose Public Library, please visit the Teens Reach: Community Service webpage for more information. Please make sure to create your online volunteer account (click "Sign Me Up" under Evergreen Branch Library) and attend an Evergreen Teens Reach meeting.
events.blurb: Join teens building leadership skills through library activities and advocacy at the Teens Reach meeting.

events.title: Bridge Card Game
events.description: Bridge is great exercise for your brain! This Bridge program is designed for adults who are passionate about Bridge and are looking to enhance their game with regular practice and social interaction. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, making it an ideal setting to engage with fellow Bridge enthusiasts and to refine your strategies. Participants should be familiar with Bridge terminology and have experience in playing the hand as instructions or assistance will not be provided. Free. Seating is limited, registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends' of the Cambrian Library!
events.blurb: Play Bridge with fellow enthusiasts in a relaxed, social setting at the library.

events.title: Willow Glen Library Knitters
events.description: Do you enjoy working with yarn, knitting or crochet? Want to see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all things yarn, knitting and crochet? All hand needle crafts welcome. No training or supplies are provided, but if you need advice there are many experienced knitters who are happy to lend a hand. Grab your project and join us weekly in the Willow Glen Library Community Room. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting or crochet project and swap tips with other yarn crafters at the library.

events.title: Las Madres Playgroup
events.description: "Nothing substitutes for the ability to build friendships with parents who are faced with similar parenting issues." Join Las Madres Downtown/Rose Garden for a weekly Tuesday playgroup. Children can play in a safe environment in the Rose Garden Library Community Room and parents can connect and find/lend support to other parents in the Rose Garden and Downtown San Jose area. Learn more about Las Madres. This is a free event. No registration is required.
events.blurb: Bring your kids to play together while parents connect and share parenting experiences at this weekly playgroup.

events.title: Crochet & Knitting Club
events.description: Do you enjoy working with yarn, knitting or crochet? Want to see what others are working on, refine your skills, talk about all things yarn, or learn how to knit or crochet? Grab your projects or supplies to start a new one and join us Tuesdays in the Vineland Library Community Room. All hand needle crafts welcome! Free. No registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Vineland Branch Library.
events.blurb: Bring your yarn project and knit or crochet alongside others at the Vineland Library community room.

events.title: Indoor Family Storytime with Stay and Play
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. After Storytime concludes, families are invited to Stay & Play! For 30 minutes after storytime, special, age-appropriate toys will be available to keep the fun going. The librarian will also be there to answer any questions, recommend books, and talk to families! Free, with limited capacity. San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime.
events.blurb: Join stories, songs, rhymes, and movement activities designed for the whole family at storytime.

events.title: English Language Learners' (ELL) Conversation Club (via Pearl and Cambrian)
events.description: San Jose Public Library presents an English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club that creates a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English conversation skills. Club meetings will convene weekly with an online meeting with our Pearl Avenue librarians and an ELL facilitator, on Tuesdays, 11:00 a.m. - 12:00 pm. Test your English skills with others who are learning English, too. Everyone is welcome! Please register by clicking on the Register button. When you give us your email, we are able to send you a link to the Zoom meeting, on the day of the program. Usually, the links will arrive about 30 minutes before the class begins.
events.blurb: Practice everyday English conversation with fellow adult learners in a relaxed weekly session at the library.

events.title: Mahjong Club
events.description: Adults and seniors interested in learning the basics or need a refresher of how to play Taiwanese Mahjong are welcome to join this program. You'll learn while playing the game: - How to set up the game tiles and understand them - The flow of the game - Make sets during the game - How to win it Learning Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress and creates a sense of community. Adults and Seniors interested in learning the basics or need a refresher of how to play Chinese Mahjong are welcome to register for this program. You'll learn while playing the game: - How to set up the game tiles and understand them - The flow of the game - Make sets during the game - How to win it Learning Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress and creates a sense of community. You will also learn strategy and strengthen communications and sense of community. No registration needed.
events.blurb: Learn to set up tiles and play Taiwanese Mahjong with other adults and seniors at Tully Library.

events.title: Games On for Older Adults
events.description: Ages 55 and up are invited to play a selection of board and card games. The games included will be a mix of strategy-based games, educational games, and luck-based games. Come together to practice strategic planning, socialization skills, and try your luck. Games include (but not limited to): Mahjong Monopoly Chess Cards *Play at your leisure. No instruction will be provided. Tickets will be distributed for a special drawing the first 10 minutes of the program. The drawing will take place near the end of the program. Light refreshments will be provided.
events.attendanceNote: Tickets will be distributed for a special drawing the first 10 minutes of the program. The drawing will take place near the end of the program.
events.blurb: Play strategy, luck, and educational board and card games with other adults 55 and up.

events.title: Music & Movement
events.description: Join us for a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. Music & Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers. San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative.
events.blurb: Sing songs, rhymes, and fingerplays with the whole family at Music & Movement, an early literacy program for all ages.

events.title: Adult Craftivities
events.description: Join us at Vineland Branch Library for some adult only craft time. Activities will change each month. This month's project is watercolor birch trees. Free. No registration required This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Vineland Branch Library.
events.blurb: Paint watercolor birch trees during adult-only craft time at Vineland Branch Library.

events.title: Creative Writing Workshop
events.description: Are you a budding creative writer? Whether you've written for years or started yesterday, register for fresh inspiration to make your story shine! Young writers, 2nd Grade to 5th Grade (ages 7-11) are invited to join us for this creative writing workshop series hosted at the Pearl Avenue Branch Library. Attendees will learn to: Write fiction that reads like reality Create characters that leave readers breathless Identify plot points that serve multiple genres This series will run from Tuesday. May 5th to Tuesday, December 15th, 2026. Please register for each session of this workshop you are looking to attend. Free. Registration is required. This program is generously sponsored by the Pearl Avenue Friends of the Library Ada Accommodations Requests

events.title: Reading to Children with Ms. Lee

Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer, Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Enjoy one-on-one or small group reading time with Ms. Lee to spark a love of books.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) - ESL 501: Reading & Writing 1
events.description: Develop your English language skills by practicing speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Do you want to build your English language skills and your confidence? This beginning non-credit ESL course is Free! ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1 What will you learn in this class? This is a non-credit, high-beginning-level integrated ESL skills course emphasizing basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will learn to comprehend frequently used words in context, use learned phrases and sentences to express ideas in basic writing, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified material. Course Information Starts: August 25, 2026 Ends: December 10, 2026 Meeting Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday Time: 10:30 AM. -12:30 PM Instructor: Michelle N. Henninger Before the classes start, you must complete a Guided Self-Placement (GSP). This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. We will assist you with the application and registration process in person at the Edenvale Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice speaking, reading, and writing English in this beginning, non-credit ESL class taught with Evergreen Valley College.

events.title: Music and Movement in Vietnamese and English and Craft/Múa Hát Song Ngữ Anh
events.description: Bilingual Music and Movement in English and Vietnamese is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities both in English and Vietnamese. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Following the Storytime, kids will learn to make a simple and creative craft to take home! On the 4th Tuesday of each month, a bilingual story will be read during this program. Free, no registration is required. Please note that this will be an indoor program. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. ADA Accommodation Requests Múa hát song ngữ bằng tiếng Anh và tiếng Việt được thiết kế để phù hợp với nhiều lứa tuổi. Chúng tôi mong muốn mời cả gia đình cùng tham gia vào các hoạt động này để cùng hát các bài đồng dao, cùng vận động ngón tay và cùng nhảy múa vui vẻ. Âm nhạc và nhảy múa là một trải nghiệm thú vị và giúp cho cả gia đình tương tác tốt hơn, thúc đẩy niềm vui học tập cho trẻ em ở mọi lứa tuổi. Mọi người đều được nhiệt liệt chào đón tại chương trình này. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Kể chuyện song ngữ và múa hát cùng với làm thủ công vào thứ ba của tuần thứ tư trong tháng. Chương trình hoàn toàn miễn phí và không cần phải đăng ký trước. ADA Yêu cầu Phương tiện để tham gia chương trình
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and move with your family in this bilingual English and Vietnamese storytime at Evergreen Library.

events.title: Bascom Teens Reach Meeting
events.description: Teens are invited to join Bascom Library Teens Reach in-person every 3rd Tuesday of the month! This program features fun volunteer opportunities, craft activities, games, and chances to hang out with your peers and learn new skills and information. To join Teens Reach you must be 13-18 years of age, have a strong interest in the library, enjoy working with people of all ages and cultures, and be willing to learn new skills. Membership requires regular attendance at meetings, participation in and support of library activities and events, and a sense of fun and adventure. As a bonus, Teens Reach members can earn community service hours through participation in meetings and activities. For more information go to: www.SJPL.org/teens Reach For ages 13-18. Held in Group Study Room 2. Registration recommended but not required.
events.blurb: Join teens for crafts, games, and volunteer opportunities at the Bascom Teens Reach meeting.

events.title: Origami for Kids
events.description: Make designs like a sailboat, penguin, frog, or samurai helmet using colorful paper. Then decorate your origami with markers! This is a self-directed program in which all supplies and instructions are made available. A staff member or volunteer will be available for assistance. Registration recommended but not required. Held in children's area. Recommended for ages 6-12. ADA Accommodation Requests Origami for the First Time Origami for Fun! Folding for Fun Origami Zoo
events.blurb: Fold colorful paper into sailboats, penguins, frogs, or samurai helmets, then decorate your creations with markers.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Our library volunteer Ms. Jenny will be available in the children's picture book area to read picture books to children. Children will have fun listening to stories while they develop a love for books and reading. Pre-registration is not required, and children may drop in to hear a story any time during the program. This program is best suited for preschoolers and children in grades K-3.
events.blurb: Listen to volunteer Ms. Jenny read picture books to kids in West Valley Library's children's area.

events.title: Rain & Water Storytime with Environmental Services

Kids will enjoy stories and activities while learning about storm drains, keeping water clean, and easy ways to save water at home. Perfect for young children and their families. Free. San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative. events.title: UC Master Gardeners: Gardening with Mediterranean Ornamentals
events.description: You may be familiar with California Native ornamental plants, but did you know that there are Mediterranean climates around the world that have the same growing conditions as we have here in Santa Clara County? Come and join UC Master Gardener Martha Carpenter to learn about beautiful, hardy, ornamental plants from other Mediterranean climates, as well as some California natives, that would be great additions to your waterwise garden! events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Some Strange Music Draws Me In
events.description: In September, the Cupertino Library Book Discussion Group will talk about the coming of age novel Some Strange Music Draws Me In: A Novel by Griffin Hansberry (2024). After their mother's death in 2019, Max and his Fox-News addicted sister work to clear out their family's home in working class Swaffham, Massachusetts. Max is currently suspended from his teaching job at a privileged private school in Massachusetts after having been accused of using transphobic language against students. Ironic, considering that Max grew up as Melanie. Stuck in a town that is less than accepting of its LGBTQIA+ community, Max reminisces about 1984, and his earlier friendship with Sylvia, a bold transgender woman who helped the girl he was then find the courage to make her transition. The Adult Book Discussion Group meets twice a month on the third Wednesday morning at 11 am, and the third Thursday Evening at 7pm. All meetings are held in room 201B. Adults of all ages are welcome. events.description: Develop your English language skills by practicing speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Do you want to build your English language skills and your confidence? This beginning non-credit ESL course is Free! ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1 What will you learn in this class? This is a non-credit, high-beginning-level integrated ESL skills course emphasizing basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will learn to comprehend frequently used words in context, use learned phrases and sentences to express ideas in basic writing, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified material. Course Information Starts: August 25, 2026 Ends: December 10, 2026 Meeting Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday Time: 10:30 AM. -12:30 PM Instructor: Michelle N. events.title: The Design of AI: Read + Learn + Craft
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Join us to read local Bay Area author Annalee Newitz's book "Automatic Noodle" (2025) set in 2064 San Francisco as we kickoff our first event of the " Crafting Our Future" series. In " The Design of AI," we'll explore themes from the novella and welcome Nina Rastogi, a writer and content designer who specializes in technology interfaces and experiences. Nina will guide us in thinking about how design shapes our interactions with AI tools and how we, in turn, can shape the tools of our future. Building on fiction and our experiences with today's technologies, we'll spend time imaging what we want 2064 to look like for us and our communities. Participants will have the opportunity to craft their vision for the future with quilting, drawing, or writing materials. Individual contributions will be collected throughout the yearlong series and turned into a vibrant patchwork exhibit. Don't miss this chance to participate in creating a tangible representation of the future we envision and what technologies and tools should look like for our community in San José and beyond. Registration is required. Light snacks will be provided. Dr. Sarah Papazoglakis is the Library's Technologist-in-Residence. She is a humanist and technologist who holds a Ph D in Literature from the University of California, Santa Cruz. She has dedicated almost a decade to designing ethical frameworks for building technology responsibly, emphasizing how storytelling and fiction are common foundations of both literature and emerging technologies like AI. "Crafting Our Future" is a year-long community conversation series that will foster thoughtful discussions around emerging technologies using texts, film, and art as a shared point of reference.

events.title: Qigong
events.description: Presenter: Amy Yang Certified Qigong Instructor International Neijin Qigong Academy Instruction will be in English and Mandarin Thursdays, August 6 through October 8, 2026 11am--12:30pm. Discover the restorative power of Qigong in this 90-minute group practice combines gentle movements, deep rhythmic breathing, and mindful focus to help reduce stress and increase vital energy. The exercises are simple, safe, and suitable for participants of all ages and fitness levels. Shaolin Neijin Yizhichan is a traditional Qigong system originating from the Southern Shaolin Temple in Fujian, China, with over 1,500 years of history. It is an effective practice for quickly enhancing internal energy and promoting spinal health. The method helps open the meridians, regulate qi and blood circulation, and restore balance between yin and yang, supporting overall physical and mental well-being, disease prevention, and longevity. events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Some Strange Music Draws Me In
events.description: In September, the Cupertino Library Book Discussion Group will talk about the coming of age novel Some Strange Music Draws Me In: A Novel by Griffin Hansberry (2024). After their mother's death in 2019, Max and his Fox-News addicted sister work to clear out their family's home in working class Swaffham, Massachusetts. Max is currently suspended from his teaching job at a privileged private school in Massachusetts after having been accused of using transphobic language against students. Ironic, considering that Max grew up as Melanie. Stuck in a town that is less than accepting of its LGBTQIA+ community, Max reminisces about 1984, and his earlier friendship with Sylvia, a bold transgender woman who helped the girl he was then find the courage to make her transition. The Adult Book Discussion Group meets twice a month on the third Wednesday morning at 11 am, and the third Thursday Evening at 7pm. All meetings are held in room 201B. Adults of all ages are welcome. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Delphian Lectures: Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties
events.description: A lecture series presented by the Delphian Study Club - providing the opportunity for lifelong learning and friendship via lectures and events. The current series: "Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties" will focus on the history and engineering of musical instruments and the composers who wrote for the instruments. Specific Lecture Topics: September 18, 2026 - Introductory class with series guest lecturer, Debora Rosengaus - Get ready, 'cause here we go! October 2, 2026 - Meet the Piano October 16, 2026 - Meet the Strings November 6, 2026 - Meet the Guitar November 20, 2026 - Meet the Brass December 4, 2026 - Meet the Woodwinds January 15, 2027 - Meet the Percussion February 5, 2027 - Meet the Conductors February 19, 2027 - Meet the Unusual Instruments March 5,2027 - Meet the Bach Family April 2, 2027 - Meet the Mozart Family April 16, 2027 - Meet the Schumann Family May 7, 2027 - Meet the Mendelssohn Siblings May 21, 2027 - Meet the Strauss Family, Waltz Kings This series will be presented by Deborah Martínez Rosengaus, a versatile Mezzo Soprano who has studied Opera, Theater, Music and Dance, and has toured internationally, with a variety of musical ensembles in concert halls such as: Santori Hall in Tokyo, The Center for Performing Arts in Beijing, Disney Hall with the Los Angeles Philharmonic, The Lincoln Center and Carnegie Hall. She has given recitals in Mexico and across the United States, giving voice to her research into the lesser-known Art Songs of great Classical composers. Ms. Rosengaus holds a Master of Music Degree from the Manhattan School of Music, where she studied with international opera diva Mignon Dunn, and a Bachelors Degree from the University of Southern California Thornton School of Music. She is the recipient of several awards including the Schoenfeld Award from the Holt Memorial Scholarship Competition and 1st place in the Pacific Musical Society Competition. She has also performed in Master classes with Karen Morrow and Luana Devol, and is a featured vocalist on several independent film soundtracks She is known for her exciting, high-energy performances and for creating memorable and endearing characters such as the role of Principessa Louling under the baton of Bruno Riggacci in the World Premier of his one act opera "Dodici personaggi in cerca di voce." Youll learn how to build basic oscillators, filters, LFOs, and amplifiers, how to rig up your circuit to be light-sensitive, and oh-so-much more. This open mic celebrates poetry in all its forms, spoken, read, sung, remembered, or improvised. Whether you write in English, Spanish, Mandarin, Hindi, Tagalog, or another language close to your heart, you are warmly invited to share. Translations and explanations are welcome but never required. All generations are encouraged to participate and attend. Come listen, come read, come perform, or simply come to be present. This is a community space rooted in respect, curiosity, and the joy of language. All are welcome. No prior experience necessary. Plan for 1 or 2 poems to share in the language of your choice (with translation or not). This could be your own poem(s) or the one(s) from an author you like. Open to poets, storytellers, elders, youth, and first-time readers alike. Let's gather to listen deeply, celebrate difference, and honor the many languages that shape our community. events.title: Dreaming with Your Eyes Open: Double Bill
events.description: Come join us in the beautiful Milpitas Library for an afternoon of surreal movies exploring social satire and self imprisonment. At 2:00 PM, we will be showing The Exterminating Angel ( El ángel exterminador), which centers around a dinner party whose guests can't seem to leave. As the night goes on the guests abandon social etiquette and fall into chaos. Created by surrealism's most influential director, Luis Buñuel, this satire is considered one of the best 1,000 movies ever made. (This movie is in Spanish with English subtitles) At 3:45 PM, we will be showing Synecdoche, New York, where Caden Cotard, an ailing theater director, tries to build a replica of the city and his life in a Manhattan warehouse in an attempt to direct it all. This program is part of the Surreal Film Series! Other events in the series: August 29: Alice in Wonderland and Fantastic Planet. October 17: The Blood of A Poet and Eraserhead.

events.title: Brain Bloom: STEAM Club
events.description: Hands-on science and art program at the Village Square Branch Library for students in grades 1-6. Brain Bloom explores the human body, nature, and the environment through engaging STEAM activities in a supportive and sensory-friendly setting. Open to all children and designed to be especially welcoming for neurodiverse learners. 8/29 -Straw Blow Painting: Explore how breathing works through using straws to blow watercolor paint across paper, creating creative shapes! The hands-on activity turns each child's breath into a colorful piece of art. 9/5 - Leaf Rubbing: Discover patterns in nature, genetics, and DNA through rubbing crayons over leaves to reveal their unique vein patterns on your paper. Then add patterns of your own, making a fascinating mix of nature and imagination. 9/12 - Emotion Masks: Learn how our brains create facial expressions and emotions, and how our neurons send messages to the rest of our body. You will then design a paper plate mask to express an emotion of your own using collage and scrapbooking techniques. 9/19 - Coffee Filter Flowers: Explore capillary action - how plants absorb water and carry it up through their stems - by coloring and water-dying coffee filters and transforming them into handmade flowers. Watch as the colors bloom right before your eyes!

events.title: Graphic Novel Making Contest Awards Ceremony
events.address: 200 East Santa Clara Street San Jose
events.description: Celebrate the creative efforts of everyone who has participated in the 2026 Graphic Novel Making Contest! Costumes and cosplay are encouraged! * All are welcome to attend, even if you didn't submit an entry. Details: Announcing Winners: Contest winners will be announced for all age groups at the Awards Ceremony. Guest Speakers: We'll have guest speakers from the comics and illustration industry! Participation Gift Pickup: All eligible participants of the Contest can claim their participation gift during the Awards Ceremony. Venue: The Awards Ceremony will be held in the San Jose City Hall Rotunda and Council Chambers. Doors open at 1:00 PM and the Ceremony begins at 2:00 PM. Parking: Free parking is available at the Fourth & St. John Garage located at 50 N. Fourth St. This program supports Summer Learning and the Graphic Novel Making Contest. *Please note prop weapons cannot be brought to the Awards Ceremony. Which items are determined as a weapon is up to the sole discretion of San Jose Public Library staff. Guest Speakers: Thien Pham Thien Pham is a graphic novelist and educator based in Oakland, CA. He is the author and illustrator of the graphic novel Sumo and the illustrator for the middle-grade graphic novel Level Up, written by Gene Luen Yang. His graphic novel, Family Style, a memoir about his family's immigration to America told through the lens of food, has been on numerous best-of lists, was a finalist for the ALA Yalsa Excellence in Non-Fiction, and won an Eisner Award for Best Memoir Graphic Novel. Pham is also the illustrator for the recurring food article on Kqed "Midnight Diners". His Latest book, which he illustrated, is Mind vs. Machine, written by Steve Sheinkin and Maurice Ashley, and will be released September 9th. Currently, Pham is working on his next graphic novel, teaching, and eating. A lot. Follow Thien on Instagram @thiendog Briana Loewinsohn Briana began making zines when she was in college in the late 90s/early 2000s. Briana mostly sold them on consignment at bay area bookstores, often making about $1.50 per book for many years. In that time, she also began teaching high school art (in 2006) and had two great kids. It wasn't until the pandemic that Briana found her voice and confidence as a cartoonist to write a full graphic novel. The book is called Ephemera, which was published in 2023. Finishing Ephemera was so exhilarating that she immediately started writing Raised By Ghosts. Raised By Ghosts won the Harvey Award and the ALA YA Non-Fiction Graphic Novel of the year. It was also nominated for an Eisner. Briana is currently working on a third graphic novel for Fantagraphics.

Spanning three dynamic sessions, this program is designed to give you a deep, practical understanding of modern AI tools and concepts: - Foundations of Language Models: Understand what a language model is and how it actually works behind the scenes. - Accuracy and Trust: Discover why AI occasionally makes mistakes and learn actionable strategies to spot inaccuracies. - Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Demystify RAG and see firsthand why grounding AI in real, verified documents drastically improves results. - Practical Application: Master simple prompts and daily habits that you can put into practice immediately. - Next-Gen Architecture: Explore the cutting-edge framework and architecture of Agentic AI. events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For September 20th: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Learn Science – Do Not Fear Death or Gods "It is impossible to get rid of our anxieties about essentials if we do not understand the nature of the universe and are apprehensive without some of the theological accounts. Hence it is impossible to enjoy our pleasures unadulterated without natural science." Principal Doctrine 12. "Dreams have neither divine character nor prophetic power but are generated by the influx of atomic images." Vatican Sayings 24. "Death means nothing to us, because that which has been broken down into atoms has no sensation and that which has no sensation is no concern of ours." Principal Doctrine 2. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Oxford University Press, 2023. Chs. 19 (pp. 202-210) and 20 (pp. 211-221); Epicurus. The Art of Happiness. Letter to Menoeceus, 123-127. Some Questions to Discuss: Why did Epicurus insist on the importance of learning science? What is Epicurus's definition of the irreligious person? What is death to us, according to Epicurus? Why would the topic of death occupy such a prominent place in the Epicurean philosophy of pleasure? Can our society be convinced by Epicurus's argument?
events.blurb: Join a friendly discussion at Rinconada Library exploring big ideas about hustle, success, and how we live.

events.title: The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) Stitch-In
events.description: The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) are hosting a friendly needle works stitch-in. Come join us from 10 am to 2 pm in the conference room, there are always extra seats! The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) chapter of the American Needlepoint Guild was chartered on March 1, 1986. We meet monthly at the Milpitas Police Department Community Room. At our meetings we present programs which encourage and inspire members to explore new techniques in needlepoint, learn about design, color, texture and perspective, and provide an opportunity to network with others who share a passion for needlepoint. The purpose of the American Needlepoint Guild is for education and cultural development through participation in and encouragement of interest in the art of needlepoint, which is defined as needlework executed by hand with a threaded needle on a readily counted ground. If you would like to find out more about SBN, please join us at one of our meetings or contact us at: sbnangcontact@gmail.com.

It is a great opportunity for people to share their favorite varieties of seeds, as well as try out new ones, share ideas, tips and tricks that go along with gardening in the local area. Bring your harvested seeds and leftover seed packets to swap with other gardeners. UC Master Gardeners will be available to answer questions about seeds. All are welcome! events.title: Bay Area Comics and Comix Exhibition
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: The California Room's exhibit "Bay Area Comics and Comix" presents the history of American comic books, highlighting the participation of the San Francisco Bay Area. The exhibit displays comic books and materials illustrating our journey from 1842's The Adventures of Obadiah Oldbuck to the arrival of the modern comic book in the 1930s, and from there to a backlash against comics in the 1950s which resulted in comic book regulation. Continuing into the 1960's, the exhibit presents the explosion of "underground" comics which were largely a Bay Area phenomenon that opened the door to the emergence of the modern graphic novel and alternative comics. Kickoff Event Join us on Saturday June 6th for the Comix and Comics Exhibition Kickoff Event! Additional Information Parking available in the SJ Park Fourth Street Garage. First 90 minutes free.
events.blurb: Browse comic books and archival materials tracing Bay Area contributions to American comic history.

events.title: Make & Decorate Sugar Skulls
events.description: Get ready for Día de los Muertos by making a sugar skull! In this multi-session program, participants will learn to make and then decorate sugar skulls using traditional and modern materials. In the first session, using a special sugar mixture and premade molds, we'll create the parts needed for a sugar skull. In the next session, after the sugar skulls have cured, we'll connect the sugar skull pieces and decorate them with colored frosting, foil, sequins, paint, and more! Once decorated, the sugar skulls will be ready to display on your home altar or our community ofrenda. Please note: creating sugar skulls is a multi-day process. Participants will not be able to finish their skulls in one session and should plan to return for the second session to decorate skulls. Session 1: Tuesday, September 22, 3:30-5:30 PM Session 2: Tuesday, September 29, 3:30-5:30 PM ¡Haz & decora tu propia Calaverita de Azúcar! ¡Ven a celebrar el Día de los Muertos creando una calaverita de azúcar muy especial! En este divertido programa de varias sesiones, aprenderás a hacer y decorar calaveritas usando materiales tradicionales y modernos. En la primera sesión, usaremos una mezcla especial de azúcar y moldes para formar las piezas de la calaverita. En la siguiente sesión, cuando ya estén listas y duritas, uniremos las piezas y las decoraremos con papel de colores, lentejuelas, pintura y mucho más. Al final, podrás llevarte tu calaverita para ponerla en tu altar en casa o en la ofrenda de la comunidad. Importante: Las calaveritas necesitan varios días para estar listas, así que no podrás terminar todo en una sola sesión. ¡Planea regresar a las siguientes para decorarlas! Sesión 1: Miércoles, 22 de septiembre, 3:30-5:30 PM Sesión 2: Miércoles, 29 de septiembre, 3:30-5:30 PM

events.title: When the Tiger Smoked a Pipe: The Art of Korea
events.description: Registration is required. Often heard at the beginning of Korean legends and folktales, "When the tiger smoked a pipe" is a familiar phrase akin to "Once upon a time." This program draws from the Asian Art Museum's collection of Korean art to explore a layered and transformative history of artmaking. Renowned for its ceramics and textiles, Korea has also created, adapted, and refined a variety of art forms. Today, Korea is among the leaders of contemporary art production. Presented by the Asian Art Museum. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.

Browse our incredible cookbook collection in the Library or our ebooks on Cloud Library or The Palace Project, find something that looks interesting to you, and cook! events.description: Busy schedules can make it difficult to practice self-care, but there are still steps you can take to do it. During this interactive and experiential workshop led by La Selva Community Clinic, participants will discuss self-care and what it means to each of us. Participants will also learn the different types of self-care, why it is essential to practice it frequently, and basic and simple things you can do to have your own self-care practice. La Selva is an adult residential and outpatient behavioral health treatment program located in Palo Alto. La Selva Community Clinic provides a full spectrum of mental health services for English and Spanish speaking adults. Registration is not required but individuals who register will receive an email reminder prior to the program.

events.title: Tech Workshop: Digital Well-Being
events.description: Worried you spend too much time on your phone? Overwhelmed by notifications and too many apps? Feeling too reliant on your smartphone for simple things? In this Digital Health workshop, you will take a closer look at your digital habits and learn practical ways to make your devices work for you, not the other way around. This adult workshop is designed for anyone who feels a little too tied to their smartphone or wants to cut back on screen time but is not sure where to start. We will explore the big picture of digital health and what that might look like for you. Then we will learn the step-by-step details that will make that vision possible. Topics include: Tracking and reducing screen time Choosing apps and exploring alternatives Reducing Distractions Social Media Breaks Privacy settings and online safety Whether you are looking for small adjustments or a larger reset, this workshop will offer approachable tools, ideas, and strategies to help you feel more intentional and in control of your digital life.
events.blurb: Take a closer look at your phone habits and learn practical ways to manage digital notifications.

events.title: Author Event: Celebrate the Mooncake Festival with Jasmine Fang
events.description: Join us for a special event featuring children's author Jasmine Fang! Jasmine will read her debut picture book, Beneath the Same Round Moon, then lead participants through a craft activity in celebration of the Autumn Moon Festival. Participants will have the chance to win a copy of Beneath the Same Round Moon (must be present to win!) There will be an author signing at the conclusion of the program. Linden Tree Books will be providing copies of Jasmine's book to purchase. Jasmine Fang is the author of Beneath the Same Round Moon (Beaming Books, September 2026) and the forthcoming Our Chinatown Market (Penguin Viking, Spring 2028). A former government and higher education professional turned author, she draws on a decade of work and travel across 30+ countries, and a lifelong love of story, to write books rooted in heart and wonder. Jasmine now lives in the San Francisco Bay Area with her husband and children. Find her online at jasmineifang.com or on Instagram @jasmineifang.
events.blurb: Hear author Jasmine Fang read Beneath the Same Round Moon, then make a Mooncake Festival craft.
